title: Cyrene founded
description: Greeks from Thera led by Battus found a colony that grows rich on grain, horses and the medicinal plant silphium.

title: Garamantes of the Fezzan
description: A Berber people of the desert oases, described by Herodotus, build a kingdom on underground irrigation and trade across the Sahara.

title: Cyrenaica left to Rome
description: Ptolemy Apion dies without an heir and leaves his kingdom to the Roman Republic.

title: Jewish revolt in Cyrene
description: A rising of the Jews of Cyrenaica spreads to Egypt and Cyprus and leaves the province devastated.

title: Septimius Severus rebuilds Leptis Magna
description: The first Roman emperor born in Africa gives his home city a new forum, basilica and harbour.

title: Earthquake and tsunami
description: An earthquake off Crete and the wave that follows wreck the cities of Cyrenaica.

title: Arabs take Tripoli
description: The army of Amr ibn al-As, having conquered Egypt and Cyrenaica, captures Tripoli and brings Islam and Arab rule to Libya.

title: Spain captures Tripoli
description: A Spanish force under Pedro Navarro storms the city, which Charles V later hands to the Knights of St John.

title: Ottomans take Tripoli
description: Sinan Pasha and Turgut Reis take the city from the Knights of St John, and Tripolitania becomes an Ottoman province.

title: Karamanli dynasty takes power
description: The cavalry officer Ahmed Karamanli seizes Tripoli and founds a dynasty that rules with little interference from Istanbul for 124 years.

title: Battle of Derna
description: American marines and hired soldiers who have marched from Egypt take the town, and Tripoli makes peace in the First Barbary War.

title: Ottoman direct rule restored
description: An Ottoman fleet removes the last Karamanli pasha, and the province is governed from Istanbul until 1911.

title: First Senussi lodge in Cyrenaica
description: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sanusi founds a lodge at Bayda, and his order becomes the main authority among the Bedouin of Cyrenaica.

title: Italian invasion
description: Italy declares war on the Ottoman Empire and lands troops at Tripoli, the start of the Italian conquest and of the first war in which aircraft drop bombs.

title: Battle of Gasr Bu Hadi
description: Senussi fighters and Libyan auxiliaries who change sides rout an Italian column, and Italy falls back to a few coastal towns.

title: Tripolitanian Republic proclaimed
description: Notables of western Libya declare a republic, the first in the Arab world, which Italy suppresses within a few years.

title: Omar al-Mukhtar hanged
description: The Italians execute the leader of twenty years of Senussi resistance before thousands of prisoners, and the conquest of Cyrenaica is complete.

title: Siege of Tobruk
description: Australian, British, Polish and other troops hold the port against Rommel for 241 days.

title: Independence
description: Under a United Nations resolution Libya becomes independent as a federal kingdom under Idris, the head of the Senussi order.

title: Oil discovered
description: Esso strikes a large oil field in the Sirte basin, and within a decade Libya is one of the world's main oil exporters.

title: Gaddafi takes power
description: Young army officers led by Muammar Gaddafi overthrow King Idris while he is abroad and declare a republic.

title: Jamahiriya declared
description: Gaddafi replaces the republic with a state of the masses run in theory by people's congresses, and in practice by himself.

title: United States bombs Tripoli and Benghazi
description: American aircraft strike Libya in reprisal for the bombing of a discotheque in West Berlin.

title: Lockerbie bombing
description: A bomb destroys Pan Am Flight 103 and kills 270 people; the attack is traced to Libyan agents, and United Nations sanctions follow.

title: Abu Salim prison massacre
description: Guards kill about 1,200 prisoners after a protest, and the families' demand for the truth later helps to start the 2011 uprising.

title: Libya gives up weapons of mass destruction
description: Gaddafi announces the end of his nuclear and chemical weapons programmes, and sanctions are lifted.

title: Uprising begins
description: Protests in Benghazi turn into an armed revolt against Gaddafi, and NATO aircraft intervene on the rebels' side in March.

title: Gaddafi killed
description: Rebel fighters capture and kill Muammar Gaddafi as his home town falls, ending his 42 years in power.

title: Attack on the United States mission in Benghazi
description: Islamist militants kill the American ambassador Christopher Stevens and three others.

title: Second civil war begins
description: Forces under Khalifa Haftar attack Islamist militias, and by the summer the country is divided between rival governments in Tripoli and Tobruk.

title: Haftar's offensive against Tripoli
description: The eastern commander orders his forces to take the capital from the government recognised by the United Nations, and the attack fails after fourteen months.
